thread:
anya: heads-up — on canary MQA build (mistral-mqa) I see what looks like KV 'laddering' over long contexts, memory steps up in stair-like increments instead of steady reuse. repro at ~1.2M tokens. attaching short logs and a perf snapshot.
lowell: can you paste the alloc trace? do you mean gradual heap growth or sudden jumps?
anya: gradual but discrete jumps every ~90-110k tokens. pages get scanned but reclaimed=0 repeatedly. here's the relevant tail: 
```
[2026-03-17T03:21:11Z] kv: pages_in_use=12480 pages_free=5120
[2026-03-17T03:23:42Z] kv: pages_in_use=12672 pages_free=4328
[2026-03-17T03:25:58Z] kv: pages_in_use=12880 pages_free=3120
[evict] scanned=4096 reclaimed=0 reason=threshold_hysteresis
```
anya: note `reason=threshold_hysteresis` logged when sweep runs.
gina: interesting — could be eviction hysteresis interacting with rope scaling for MQA. MQA changes token grouping so KV slot lifetimes differ; if kernel selector flips between GQA/MQA kernels we might be allocating slightly different page shapes and never coalescing.
mike: do we have a recent kernel-switch event around deploy time? might be kernel churn -> allocator fragmentation.
evict-bot: rollout: mistral-mqa-kernel-v2 deployed to canary at 2026-03-16T03:12:44Z; metric: small increase in avg page_allocs/sec (+7%).
lowell: ok that matches. hypothesis: kernel v2 uses 64-byte-aligned page subblocks vs v1 48b -> fragmentation laddering when requests mix old/new kernels across the same runtime. also eviction hysteresis threshold is currently 0.25 which delays reclamation until we cross next stair.
sanjay: to reproduce locally: run bench/longctx.py --model mistral-mqa --seq 131072 --clients 8 --duration 2h --profile-kv. add env `KV_EVICT_HYSTERESIS=0.0` to force immediate reclamation and compare.
anya: ran that config with hyst=0.0 — laddering disappears, pages oscillate but reclaimed counts >0. so hysteresis is a big factor. with default hysteresis we still see steady step ups.
gina: we should also confirm kernel selector path: add `--kernel-trace=on` to bench; if selector toggles for certain seq lengths that will align with those token counts. Qwen and Llama historically behave differently; MQA-specific grouping makes this more visible.
mike: quick mitigation: bump sweep aggressiveness and lower hysteresis to 0.15 for canary and monitor. longer-term: make page format stable across kernel variants or run lazy coalescer that can merge subblocks from mixed kernels.
lowell: agree. I'll open an RFC for "stable page layout across kernel families" and track tradeoffs.
anya: I'll flip canary to hyst=0.15 now and run the 2h longctx, post results. thanks all :thumbsup:
